description: Two-part, fully printed wall enclosure for an ESP32-2432S028R ("Cheap Yellow Display") heating and hot-water controller that replaces a Danfoss FP720 programmer. The base tray locates the relay board, Hi-Link PSU and WAGO block behind a partition rib that keeps the mains bay apart from the low-voltage display wiring, and carries a stylus sleeve on its right-hand side. The faceplate frames the display and carries two Hand-Off-Auto toggles and two indicator lamps. Every fixing uses an M3 heat-set insert.

hardware.item: ESP32-2432S028R display board (Cheap Yellow Display) with its stylus
Hi-Link HLK-10M05B AC-DC PSU on stripboard with a 2x2 screw terminal
XURUI XT-13A SPDT centre-off toggle switch
hardware.notes: Hand-Off-Auto, one per circuit; 12 mm keyed panel hole
Amber for heating, blue for hot water; 10 mm panel hole assumed

hardware.item: M3 heat-set insert (4.6 mm OD, up to 5.7 mm long)

printing_notes: Print in PETG or ASA with 3 perimeters, in the exported orientation, without supports.
Press the heat-set inserts in with a soldering iron before fitting the boards. Support the lid face flat while pressing the CYD inserts, because only about 1.2 mm of skin is behind them.
Without inserts, set insert_hole_d to 2.6 and use self-tapping screws; the lid screws then become 3 mm self-tappers.
Test the toggle hole fit and adjust toggle_hole_d by 0.2 mm either way. Confirm toggle_key_w and the lamp cut-out before the final print.
Shift the display window with window_off_x and window_off_y, and adjust cyd_display_h, after a test fit.
The stylus drops cap-up into the right-hand sleeve and pushes out through the open bottom.
Fix the base to the wall before fitting the PSU and the relay board, which sit over two of the wall screws.
Leave the relay NC screw terminals empty.
